1.explanation: packages/react/src/components/Tile/Tile.js houses the SelectableTile component, including getDerivedStateFromProps, handleClick, and handleKeyDown. The bug originates here because handleClick always inverts the incoming prop instead of reading the updated selected prop after a Shift‐click range update. This logic causes a tile that should remain selected to toggle off. The accompanying test file (Tile-test.js) needs to be updated to cover the Shift+click multi‐select scenario and ensure the component honors the selected prop rather than solely toggling internal state.
1.bug_scenario: When a user performs a range‐selection by holding the Shift key and clicking on a SelectableTile, the last tile in the range—if it was already selected—gets deselected. The component’s handleClick (and handleKeyDown) unconditionally invert this.props.selected rather than respecting the updated prop value provided by a parent (e.g. TileGroup’s range selection), so the visible selected state falls out of sync with the selected prop.

2.explanation: All of the selection-toggle logic for the React and vanilla-JS versions of the Tile lives in these two files. In packages/react/src/components/Tile/Tile.js the SelectableTile’s `handleClick` and `handleKeyDown` methods invert `this.props.selected` instead of respecting the updated prop value when performing a multi-select with Shift+click, leading to a stale local state. The companion vanilla JS implementation in packages/components/src/components/tile/tile.js also handles click/toggle on the same underlying `<input>` and needs to mirror the fix so that range-select never inverts a stale state.
2.bug_scenario: When you hold Shift and click on a previously selected SelectableTile to do a multi-selection, the tile briefly deselects itself (the local component state flips) even though the parent’s `selected` prop is still `true`. In other words, on Shift+click the last tile is toggled out of sync with the props coming from your application’s state, so it loses its visual “selected” styling even though it should remain selected.
